 Christine Burroni Wed, October 21, 2026 at 9:08 PM UTC 3 min read Add Yahoo as a preferred source to see more of our stories on Google. The royal family marked the anniversary of a major tragedy in UK history on Wednesday, which the late Queen Elizabeth reportedly regretted her handling of at the time.
 Visiting the mining village of Aberfan, Wales — where 116 children and 28 adults were killed after a hillside of coal waste slid down onto a primary school and nearby homes on Oct. 21, 1966 — King Charles, Queen Camilla, and Prince William paid tribute to the site of the horrifying incident by meeting with survivors as well as the parents of victims.
 However, in the immediate aftermath of what is now known as the Aberfan disaster, the queen was reportedly advised not to visit with the thinking that she and her entourage would cause too much of a commotion for a town in mourning amid its ongoing rescue efforts. She instead sent her husband, Prince Philip, and Princess Margaret 's husband, Lord Snowdon , to represent her, according to the BBC. 
 Advertisement Advertisement Advertisement Advertisement The late monarch was criticized for what seemed like a lack of urgency to visit with the grieving families and made her way to Aberfan eight days later. She later reportedly referred to the delay in her visit as "the biggest regret of her reign."
 The Queen visiting Aberfan days after tragedy struck. Evening Standard / Getty Images
 The queen, who was 40 years old at the time and had two young children, in addition to the then-Prince Charles and Princess Anne, was said to be visibly emotional when visiting with grief-stricken parents. (The former Prince Andrew and Prince Edward were of similar age to the children that had been killed.)
 "To me that day, she didn't come as the Queen, our monarch, she came as a mother, to sympathize, to empathize, to really appreciate what everybody had been through that day," a mourner recounted to the BBC in 2022.
 The late monarch returned to the village in 1997 and planted a commemorative tree in its Garden of Remembrance and met with survivors. Her final visit to the site was in 2012.
 On Wednesday, the king made a speech during his visit with his wife and son to honor the victims.
 Advertisement Advertisement "Over the years, as once again today, it has been profoundly humbling to hear the testimonies of survivors of relatives who lost their loved ones, and of rescuers who fought so hard to save others during this appalling tragedy," he said, according to the BBC. "Today in our nation and across the world, thoughts will turn to you in Aberfan, hearts far from this valley will ache with yours."
 William also laid a commemorative wreath down at the site of where the school once stood.
